We need answer user: "Explain why local inference benchmarks should report prompt prefill throughput, decode throughput, and time to first token." Need provide explanation. Need final answer. Need likely discuss LLM inference phases: prefill/prompt processing vs decode token generation. Local benchmarks need these metrics because they capture different bottlenecks: prefill throughput (tokens/s for prompt) measures how fast model can process input context, KV cache build, attention over prompt, batched prompt, memory bandwidth/compute, affects latency for long contexts and RAG. Decode throughput (tokens/s generated) measures autoregressive generation speed, often memory-bandwidth bound, affects sustained output speed. TTFT (time to first token) measures user-perceived latency from request to first generated token, includes prompt prefill, scheduling, loading, overhead; important for interactive use. Reporting all three avoids misleading single throughput number: a model may have high decode but slow prefill, or low TTFT but poor sustained throughput; local hardware varies (CPU/GPU, quantization, batch size, context length). Also prompt length and output length matter; need separate metrics to diagnose bottlenecks and compare systems fairly. Could mention prefill throughput can be high due to parallelism but not reflect interactive latency; decode throughput can be high in batch but not single-stream; TTFT captures end-to-end first token. Also local inference: resource constraints, no cloud, users care about responsiveness and total time. Need maybe include formulas: prefill throughput = prompt tokens / prefill time; decode throughput = generated tokens / decode time; TTFT = time from request to first token. Also mention total time = TTFT + (n-1)/decode throughput approx. Need explain why not just tokens/s. Maybe include examples: long prompt short answer vs short prompt long answer. Also local benchmarks should report context length, batch size, quantization, hardware, because metrics depend. Need answer concise but thorough.
</think>

Local inference benchmarks should report **prompt prefill throughput**, **decode throughput**, and **time to first token (TTFT)** because LLM inference has distinct phases with different performance characteristics, and a single “tokens per second” number can be misleading.

### 1. Prompt prefill throughput
**Prefill** is the phase where the model processes the input prompt and builds the key-value cache.

- Measures how quickly the system can handle long contexts.
- Often compute-bound, especially on GPUs.
- Important for RAG, chat history, code
